newsitem.title: USA: Murdoch buys IFE as industry consolidates further.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch buys IFE as industry consolidates further.

text.p: Tim Robertson, the man who will serve as president of the latest company acquired by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, said on Wednesday that the decision to sell was a decision to join an industry-wide consolidation process.
"It was really time to join the consolidation that was going on in the industry," said Robertson in an interview broadcast on Fox News Channel, also owned by News Corp.

Robertson, along with his father, Christian evangelist Pat Robertson, announced earlier in the day that their International Family Entertainment Inc media company was bought by a unit of News Corp in a deal valued at $1.9 billion.
Under the terms of the deal, News Corp's Fox Kids Worldwide Inc unit, a children's programming arm of the Murdoch media empire, will pay $35 a share in cash for IFE.
"We insisted on a deal that was fair to all shareholders," the younger Robertson said. "The easiest thing for everyone was cash."

When asked how IFE's Family Channel would be affected by the deal, Robertson said programming would benefit from News Corp's partnerships with Scholatic Corp, a publisher of children's books, and Marvel Entertainment Group Inc, and he hoped to see the channel become a global brand.
